## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## Why

Mirror creation currently depends on the synchronous placement endpoint, which holds the request open while placement work completes. The control plane now exposes asynchronous mirror-request routes so the CLI can submit placement, observe its state, and then continue through the existing initial-clone wait.

## What changed

Add generated client support for the mirror-request routes and let normal layered repository settings select the asynchronous flow. One-shot and wizard creation share the same submit, placement poll, and clone poll path, including cross-jurisdiction token exchange and bounded transient-error handling.

## Usage examples

Enable the route in `.entire/settings.json`, with `.entire/settings.local.json` available as the usual local override:

```json
{
  "async_mirror_requests": true
}
```

`entire repo mirror create github.com/owner/repo aws-us-east-2.entire.io` then reports queued, placing, and cloning progress. With `--no-wait`, it waits for placement and returns the assigned mirror URL without waiting for the initial clone.

## Decisions made during development

- The setting is default-off and follows normal project/local layering.
- Selecting the async route does not preflight capability or fall back to the synchronous endpoint. An unavailable route remains visible as an error.
- If repository settings cannot be loaded by this control-plane-exempt command, creation retains the default synchronous route.
- The existing two-second clone poll and 15-consecutive-error tolerance remain unchanged, including the post-placement visibility window.
- A single timeout covers async submission, placement, and initial clone readiness.
- Async results report the contract-backed mirror URL without guessing whether placement was fresh or idempotent.

## Technical tradeoffs

Sync and async creation coexist during rollout. This keeps the current production path unchanged by default, at the cost of carrying both routes until the async path is ready to become universal.

content.text:
Review's done — 15 findings. I independently verified the mechanism behind the top ones against the merged code before relaying. Since #2207 is already on main, these are follow-up work rather than blockers.

## Real bugs

**1. `Suspended` is silently dropped on the async path** — `repo_mirror_probe.go:133`

`awaitMirrorPlacement` synthesizes its `CreatedMirror` from three fields:

```go
return &coreapi.CreatedMirror{
    MirrorId:  result.MirrorId,
    MirrorUrl: result.MirrorUrl,
    PublicUrl: result.PublicUrl,
}, nil
```

`MirrorRequestResult` has no `Suspended` field at all, but both consumers branch on it — `repo_mirror.go:629` and `repo_mirror_create_wizard.go:581`. So `create --no-wait` against an admin-suspended placement prints "Initial clone may still be in progress" and **exits 0**, where the sync route prints the warning and exits non-zero via `NewSilentError(errMirrorSuspended)`. `TestCreateOneMirror_Suspended` hand-builds `CreatedMirror{Suspended: true}`, so it only covers the sync shape. Cleanest fix: add the field to the contract, or don't return early on `noWait` without a status read.

**2. Cross-juris placement polling breaks after ~4 minutes** — `repo_mirror_probe.go:112`

`awaitMirrorPlacement` sets `WithServerURL(homeCore)` so polls go straight to the home core with no 421 hop. But the home core's bare-401 recovery in `cross_juris_transport.go:267` is gated on `budget.afterRedirect`, and `retryBudget` is constructed fresh per `RoundTrip` (line 182) — so with the redirect optimized away, `afterRedirect` is always false. Within `cachedTokenTTL` (4 min) the cached exchanged token carries it; past that, `lookupToken` misses, the poll goes out with the original login JWT, the home core 401s with no hint, and `if !budget.afterRedirect { return resp, nil }` passes it through unrecovered. 15 consecutive 401s later the command dies while the placement is fine. `awaitMirrorReady` is immune *only because it wasn't given the override* — i.e. the optimization is strictly worse than not having it.

**3. A missing or prefixed `Location` hard-fails a succeeded placement** — `repo_mirror_probe.go:107`

`mirrorRequestPollTarget(location)` runs before anything looks at `initial.Status`. `Location` is optional in the spec, `RequestId` is required, and `GetMirrorRequestParams` needs only the id — so a server that omits the header, or emits it without the `/api/v1` prefix, gets `mirror request response is missing Location` even when the 202 body already carries a finished mirror. The strict `initial.RequestId != requestID` cross-check has the same shape.

## Hardening

**4. `mirrorRequestPollTarget` accepts `http://<any host>`** (`:188`) — the check is `Scheme != "https" && Scheme != "http"`, unlike `coreapi.isSafeOrigin`, which allows http only for loopback precisely because these paths re-target the login JWT. Production is saved solely by `canonicalizeMirrorRequestLocation` overwriting scheme+host — which is gated on `req.URL.Path == apiBasePath+"/mirror-requests"`, so a core served under a path prefix skips it entirely and a hostile `Location` becomes the `WithServerURL` base. Neither function names the other as its precondition, in a file where every other trust gate is documented explicitly.

**5. `canonicalizeMirrorRequestLocation` has no doc comment** (`cross_juris_transport.go:308`) and unconditionally rewrites the host — so an intentionally off-host `Location` gets pointed back at the responding core, which may 404 the request id until the error budget drains.

## Robustness / UX

- **Request id discarded on timeout** (`repo_mirror.go:625`): `return mirrorCreateOutcome{}, err` throws away `accepted.Response.RequestId`, and there's no `mirror request get` subcommand — so a placement timeout leaves no handle to resume or inspect. The sync route never had this hole.
- **Unreachable `default:` branch** (`:141`): `MirrorRequestStatus.UnmarshalText` returns `invalid value` on anything outside the 4-value enum, so a new server status fails at decode and gets swallowed by the 15-error budget instead of producing the intended message. This contradicts the operation's own "unknown failure codes must be treated as generic terminal failure" contract, which the code *does* honor for `failure.code`.
- **Flag semantics are now route-dependent** (`:539`): `--no-wait` still says "without waiting for the initial clone" but blocks in `awaitMirrorPlacement` up to the full 30m timeout on the async route; `--wait-timeout`'s broadened help is now wrong for sync, where `waitCtx` gets no deadline at all (`if opts.async && opts.timeout > 0`) — a hanging sync `CreateMirror` is unbounded.
- **Three `✓` lines for one create** (`:525`): each phase starts a new spinner instead of relabeling one via the existing `startUpdatableSpinner`, and `stop(true)` writes `✓` on both TTY and non-TTY. Queued gets a `✓` even when placement then fails.
- **Wizard reports `error` vs `timed out`** by phase (`wizard:607`): `mirrorStatusTimedOut` is only reachable once `outcome.created != nil`, so the same timeout renders two ways depending on which half of one window it landed in.

## Worth a product call

**The rollout switch lives in repo-committed `.entire/settings.json`** (`repo_mirror.go:493`). `entire repo mirror create` is normally run *before* the repo exists locally, so the key silently has no effect where the command is most used — and the load error is swallowed (`if ... err == nil`), so nothing says why. Conversely, any repo can flip which control-plane route every contributor uses while they stand in it. The `repo` group is `.entire`-exempt precisely because it doesn't depend on repo state; per-user config or an env var fits better.

## Hygiene

Three comment deletions I confirmed in the diff: `maxConsecutivePollErrors` lost the measured `minimize_latency + follower reads (~4.8s)` window, the 15×2s arithmetic, and the named CRDB-leaseholder fix that would retire it — now that the constant is shared by a second poll phase with a different failure profile. `createAndAwaitMirror` lost the doc comment stating the error contract both callers still branch on. The four new functions ship undocumented. `/api/v1` is hardcoded twice in `mirrorRequestPollTarget`, duplicating the unexported `coreapi.apiBasePath`. And `t.Parallel()` was dropped from `session_store_test.go:144` — correct, since it reads `/proc/self/fd`, but unexplained and unmentioned in an otherwise mirror-scoped PR, so the next reader will restore it.

I haven't posted anything to the PR. Want me to file the top three as issues, draft a PR comment, or publish this as a shareable page for pfleidi?

Full picture — the PR is fine, but the ground moved under it.

## PR #2242: open, green, unapproved

Every CI check passes. **Entire Gates** shows fail, but only on the Approvals sub-gate — "No reviewers have approved this trail". Checks passed, and the Findings gate passed ("Agent review found no blocking issues"). So there's nothing to fix there; it needs a human.

## Two bot findings, both real, both mine

- **Cursor Bugbot (medium):** my "The mirror request was accepted … and may still be progressing / re-run the same command" notice fires whenever `requestID` is set and there's no placement — but `requestID` is also set for a terminal **failed** placement. So a `repo_inaccessible` failure now prints a failure *and* tells the user to re-run. Genuine bug I introduced; the notice needs gating on non-terminal outcomes.
- **Copilot (nit):** my comment edit left a stray `createAndAwaitMirror: a` line break in `repo_mirror.go`. That's from the wording fix I made late — it reads like a typo.

## The bigger problem: the branch is 164 commits behind, and two premises expired

`git merge-tree` gives three conflicts, and two are substantive rather than mechanical:

**1. `cross_juris_transport.go` was deleted on main.** The whole cross-jurisdiction transport moved into the shared `auth-go crossjuris` package (`02abf214b`), leaving a thin `cross_juris_client.go`. Critically, **`canonicalizeMirrorRequestLocation` survived that refactor** — it was deliberately rebuilt as a `mirrorLocationCanonicalizer` RoundTripper wrapping the shared follower, with new doc comments explaining it rewrites onto "the origin that actually answered" so it works after the replay. My PR deletes that function on the grounds nothing consumes the Location any more. That premise still holds if my probe change lands, but someone has since invested in the thing I'm removing, so it's a conversation now, not a rebase. My doc comments also cite `retryBudget.afterRedirect` and `cross_juris_transport.go` — both gone.

**2. PR #2246 turned async mirror creation on by default.** Main now has `opts.async = true` as the default with `IsAsyncMirrorRequestsEnabled()` reading a tri-state `*bool`, plus commits "Preserve async mirror opt-out" and "Keep async default on settings errors". Two consequences:

- Every bug #2242 fixes is **no longer behind a default-off flag** — the suspended-placement exit-0, the cross-juris 4-minute polling death, the unbounded sync timeout are all live for everyone now. That makes this PR more urgent than when I opened it.
- My finding-10 fix partly collides. They restructured the setting themselves and chose the *opposite* failure direction: on a settings error they keep async, where I warn and fall back to sync. My `resolveAsyncMirrorRequests` also returns `s.AsyncMirrorRequests` as a `bool`, which won't compile against the new `*bool`.

## What I'd do

Rebase onto main, and in the process: fix the two bot findings; drop my env-var/settings work in favour of main's tri-state shape (keeping only the "don't swallow the load error" half, adapted to their default-on choice); and **keep `canonicalizeMirrorRequestLocation` deleted but say so explicitly in the PR** so whoever did the auth-go refactor can push back — the argument for removing it is that nothing reads the header once the poll runs off `requestId`, and it's dead weight plus a trust surface otherwise.

Want me to do that rebase, or would you rather ping pfleidi on the default-on overlap first?

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"; git commit -q --amend -F - <<'MSG'
Fix async mirror-create review findings from #2207

Since #2246 made the async route the default, these are live for everyone
rather than gated behind an opt-in flag.

Drives the placement poll off the 202 body's requestId instead of the
Location header, which removes three problems at once: an optional header
no longer fails a create whose body already reports success, no
server-named host can become a poll target for the control-plane bearer,
and the poll keeps 421ing to the home core so the transport's bare-401
re-exchange stays recoverable past the token cache. With nothing reading
the header, the mirrorLocationCanonicalizer that maintained it goes too —
it survived the auth-go/crossjuris refactor in 02abf214b, but its only
consumer is gone.

Restores parity between the two routes: MirrorRequestResult carries no
`suspended` field, so an async create against a suspended placement
reported plain success and exited 0 where the sync route warns and exits
non-zero. One status read fills it in for every caller.

Makes --wait-timeout cover submission, placement and clone on both
routes. It previously bounded only the clone poll on the sync route, so a
hanging CreateMirror ignored the flag; the help text documented that
split rather than fixing it.

Also: an accepted request's id survives a wait that ended with no verdict,
so the user has a handle on in-flight work — but not a terminal failure,
which is done and must not be described as still progressing; the wizard
labels a placement timeout "timed out" rather than "error"; one
relabelled spinner replaces three per-phase spinners that each stamped
their own check mark; and ENTIRE_ASYNC_MIRROR_REQUESTS overrides the
route in both directions, since this command usually runs outside the
repo whose settings.json holds the opt-out. A settings-load error is now
reported instead of swallowed, without changing the route — a read that
failed is not evidence the repo opted out.

Restores the poll-budget and createAndAwaitMirror rationale comments
dropped in #2207, documents the new functions and the unreachable
unknown-status branch, and records why the session-store FD test is
deliberately not parallel.
